newsitem.title: USA: World Bank-Vietnam needs $4 bln foreign investment.
newsitem.headline: World Bank-Vietnam needs $4 bln foreign investment.

text.p: Vietnam needs about $4 billion in outside funding, mostly in the form of foreign direct investment, to help it continue needed economic structural reforms, the World Bank said Friday in a report.
It said development assistance is needed to update infrastructure to support private sector development and investment in social services, particularly in rural areas.

"Sustaining rapid growth and poverty reduction in Vietnam will require an efficient and equitable economy based on continued macroeconomic stability, structural reforms and the successful delivery of basic rural services," the Bank said.

The report said that to achieve targeted growth of 9 to 10 percent, Vietnam will need to continue developing competitive, export-oriented agriculture and industrial sectors. It also needs to increase investment through rising domestic savings.

It gave high marks for achieving impressive economic growth of eight percent a year over the past five years, and noted that inflation has been reduced to about three percent in 1996 due to tight fiscal and monetary policies as well as falling food prices. However, it said that it was unlikely that this could be sustained at such a low level in the future.
